questions.q: What causes the vanishing gradient problem in a plain RNN trained on long sequences?
options: The optimizer's learning rate is always set too low
Repeated multiplication by tanh/sigmoid derivatives (almost always < 1) across many timesteps shrinks the gradient toward zero
PyTorch rounds small floating-point numbers to zero automatically
The input data was not normalized
questions.explain: Backpropagation through time multiplies many derivatives under 1 together, so gradient signal from early timesteps shrinks exponentially by the time it's needed.

questions.q: What is the key structural difference that lets the LSTM's cell state avoid vanishing as badly as a plain RNN's hidden state?
options: The cell state is updated additively (a sum), not through a repeated chain of multiplications
The cell state uses a larger learning rate than the hidden state
The cell state is recomputed from scratch at every timestep with no memory
The cell state only exists during inference, not training
questions.explain: c_t = f_t * c_{t-1} + i_t * g_t is an additive update, so gradients can flow backward through the + without being forced through a long multiplicative chain.

questions.q: In nn.LSTM, what do the forget, input, and output gates control, respectively?
options: Learning rate, batch size, and number of layers
How much old cell state survives, how much new info is added, and how much of the cell state is exposed as the hidden state
Which optimizer to use, which loss function to use, and which activation to use
The three different hidden layers of the network
questions.explain: Forget decides what to keep from c_{t-1}, input decides how much new candidate information g_t to add, and output decides how much of c_t becomes h_t.

questions.q: Calling nn.LSTM returns output, (h_n, c_n). What is c_n?
options: The loss value at the final timestep
The final cell state — the LSTM's long-term memory at the end of the sequence
A copy of the input tensor
The gradient computed during the forward pass
questions.explain: Unlike nn.RNN, nn.LSTM carries two states: h_n (final hidden state, what it exposes) and c_n (final cell state, its long-term memory).

questions.q: What is the 'exploding gradient' problem, and how does it relate to vanishing gradients?
options: It's unrelated — a completely separate bug caused only by bad data
It's the opposite failure mode from the same chain of repeated multiplications, where gradients grow instead of shrink, usually handled with gradient clipping
It only happens in CNNs, never in recurrent networks
It means the model's accuracy exploded upward unexpectedly
questions.explain: The same long chain of multiplications that can shrink gradients toward zero can, under different conditions, cause them to grow instead — addressed later in this course with gradient clipping.
